basic_info: Three-year-old female presenting with a twitch in her right eye noticed by her father a couple of weeks ago.
present_illness: The patient reports a twitch in her right eye, which was first noticed by her father a couple of weeks ago. The twitch occurs a few times an hour, lasts a few seconds, and is more noticeable in the late afternoon. The patient describes it as feeling like her face wants to move, and she feels better after it happens. The twitch is localized to the right side of the face and does not involve blinking or other facial movements. The patient denies headaches, visual changes, or trouble with coordination. She has been eating well, playing with friends, and going to soccer every Saturday. She does not think anything else has changed recently except for the twitch. The patient denies experiencing fatigue, stress, or unusual movements besides the eye twitch. She also denies any changes in vision or eye movement patterns. The patient has not experienced any recent changes in sleep patterns, dietary habits, or exposure to new medications or environmental factors. The patient mentions that the twitch seems to happen more when she is tired, like later in the day, and sometimes after playing soccer. It does not really bother her when it happens, and she does not notice it getting worse when she is excited or after eating something specific. Dad says he notices it more in the afternoons, but she just keeps doing what she is doing.
past_history: The patient's father reports no family history of seizures, Tourette's syndrome, or other movement disorders. The patient denies any other involuntary movements and the absence of vision changes or eye movement abnormalities.
physical_exam: Physical examination was unremarkable with no focal neurological deficits. Pupils were equal, round, and reactive to light. No ptosis or ophthalmoplegia noted. No signs of facial weakness or abnormal movements. Vital signs were within normal limits. Cranial nerve examination was intact. Motor and sensory examinations were normal. Reflexes were symmetric and within normal limits.
aux_exam: No relevant auxiliary examinations have been performed yet.
